question: Why did airport travellers give money after being handed a flower they never asked for?
answer: Because of the rule of reciprocity: we feel obliged to repay what others give us, even an unwanted gift. Robert Cialdini describes members of the Hare Krishna movement pressing a flower into travellers' hands and then asking for a donation. Many gave, and many then threw the flower away.
move: A gift you didn't ask for is often a debt someone wants repaid.
simply: When a friend gives you a sweet, you feel you should give one back, even if you didn't want the first one.
why: Free samples, 'free' consultations and small favours work the same way. Noticing the pull lets you decide on the request alone.
reference: Robert B. Cialdini, Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion (William Morrow, 1984), ch. 2
